summary: The study fabricated eight distinct Ti3C2Tx fiber-electrode materials: a pure L-Ti3C2Tx control, four Ti3C2Tx-QD/L-Ti3C2Tx composition ratios spun in chitosan, and three Q3M7 fibers made using alternative coagulation baths. L-Ti3C2Tx was produced by natural-sedimentation size selection of Ti3AlC2, LiF/HCl etching, and mechanical delamination; Ti3C2Tx QDs were produced by ultrasonication. The headline Q3M7 fiber, made in 5 wt.% chitosan, delivered the best reported electrode volumetric capacitance, 1560 F cm−3 at 1 A cm−3 in 1 M H2SO4. The assembled F-MMT/PVA DHGE Q3M7 fiber-supercapacitor is a device using the same Q3M7 electrodes, rather than an additional electrode material; it reported 413 F cm−3 at 0.5 A cm−3. Electrode thickness, mass loading, BET area, pore dimensions, porosity, and numerical capacitances for Q1M9, Q2M8, and Q4M6 were not printed.
